newsitem.title: UK: Bill and Tony wrap up show with $150 champagne.
newsitem.headline: Bill and Tony wrap up show with $150 champagne.

text.p: The "Bill and Tony Show" wrapped up a triumphant one-day performance with a $150 bottle of champagne at an exclusive London riverside restaurant on Thursday night to put the seal on a deepening friendship.

And as U.S. President Bill Clinton and British Prime Minister Tony Blair raised their glasses in the sunset, there was little doubt that the so-called special relationship between London and Washington was back in vogue.

British officials said the two leaders and their wives had started off with a 92-pound ($150) bottle of Bollinger 1989 champagne before tucking into a hefty meal at the ritzy Le Pont de La Tour restaurant on the banks of the Thames.
Bill Clinton chose roast wild salmon and Tony Blair had the roast leg of rabbit, while both women opted for fish -- the Dover sole going to Hillary Clinton and the fillet of halibut to Cherie Blair.
"The conversation was personal and (focused on) what life is like in the fishbowl. They also swapped interesting ideas," White House spokesman Mike McCurry told reporters outside.
It was the fitting end to a remarkable day which began when the Blairs greeted their guests warmly on the steps of No 10 Downing Street, where both couples beamed and shook hands for the cameras.
"Tony's new best friend drops in," was the headline in the London Evening Standard.
Such friendliness on the part of a British premier would have been improbable during the tenure of Blair's predecessor John Major, whose relations with Clinton were rocky.

Clinton was accorded the rare honour of being invited to address the cabinet, and surprised ministers by disclosing that he was familiar with key passages of the Labour party manifesto that helped Blair to power in his landslide May 1 election victory.

After being applauded as he entered the cabinet room, Clinton declared with a laugh that he did not have much advice to pass on to a prime minister who had just won a thumping 179-seat majority in the House of Commons.
"I'm not going to give advice, I'm going to sit here and get it," he said.
Blair quickly praised the man on whose campaigning successes he had modelled his own march to power, saying that Clinton did have one thing to show him -- how to get re-elected.

After talks and lunch -- and while Hillary and Cherie went off to watch some Shakespeare -- Clinton and Blair moved into the sunlit Downing Street rose garden where the mutual admiration stepped up a gear.
"I've already seen part of what I wanted to see, a most unique and unspeakably beautiful British spring," said Clinton, who knows the country well from his student days.
The two were pressed about their similarities -- they are both Oxford-educated rock fans married to high-flying lawyers and Blair has been described by critics as a Clinton clone.
Clinton, forced to walk with a silver-topped cane because of a knee injury, joked that he was different from the 44-year-old Blair in one important respect.
"I do resent this because he is seven years younger than me with no grey hairs."
